dnssec_validation.title: DNSSEC Validation Mode
dnssec_validation.description: BIND 9 'dnssec-validation' option (named.conf.options). Whether the resolver cryptographically validates DNSSEC signatures on answers — the primary defense against cache poisoning / spoofed answer-record injection for signed zones. Secure: auto or yes (signatures validated). Insecure: no — signatures unchecked, forged records accepted into the cache.

named_below_cve_fix_line.title: named Build Below CVE Fix Line
named_below_cve_fix_line.description: Interpreted boolean: true when the running BIND 9 (named) build is BELOW the relevant ISC fix line for a known remotely-exploitable advisory — cache poisoning CVE-2025-40778 (fixed 9.18.41 / 9.20.15 / 9.21.14, or -S1 preview equivalents) plus resource-exhaustion DoS CVEs (CVE-2024-12705 / CVE-2025-8677 / CVE-2024-11187). Such builds are overly lenient in accepting answer records, letting a remote off-path attacker inject forged domain->IP mappings into the cache, and are exposed to remotely-triggerable DoS. Modeled as an interpreted boolean because the security state is a semantic version comparison, not a substring match.

named_patched_within_sla.title: named Patched Within SLA
named_patched_within_sla.description: Shared cross-component patch-cadence facet: the named process is running a release on or after the relevant ISC security-advisory fix line within the organisation's patch SLA. Secure value is true (a patched build); the exposure fires when false (an out-of-SLA build is exposed to the modeled poisoning/DoS CVEs). Mirrors edge_appliance_patched_within_sla / cache_patched_within_sla used elsewhere in the workspace.

open_recursion_enabled.title: Open Recursion Enabled
open_recursion_enabled.description: Interpreted from BIND 'recursion' in named.conf.options: true when the server performs recursive resolution (recursion yes;) — the precondition for open-resolver reflection abuse. An authoritative-only server should have recursion no; (false). True alone is not the exposure; combined with an unrestricted allow-recursion ACL or absent DDoS mitigation it makes the server an open recursive resolver abusable as a DNS amplification reflector.

recursion_acl_unrestricted.title: Recursion ACL Unrestricted
recursion_acl_unrestricted.description: Interpreted from BIND 'allow-recursion' in named.conf.options: true when recursion is offered to untrusted clients — allow-recursion { any; } or no allow-recursion clause while recursion yes; is set. The assessor reads the address-match list rather than substring-matching the raw directive (a trusted ACL like { 10.0.0.0/8; localnets; } is secure → false). True means any spoofed-source client can drive recursive queries, turning the resolver into a reflector for amplification/reflection DDoS.

ddos_protection_in_place.title: DDoS Protection In Place
ddos_protection_in_place.description: Shared-vocabulary attestation: true when effective volumetric/reflection DDoS mitigation is in place for this DNS service (e.g. BIND Response Rate Limiting via a rate-limit{} block, upstream anti-spoofing/BCP38 ingress filtering, or a scrubbing/anycast tier). False means an open recursive resolver has no rate or volume control, so spoofed-source small queries yield large responses flooding a third-party victim unchecked.

response_rate_limiting_enabled.title: Response Rate Limiting Enabled
response_rate_limiting_enabled.description: Interpreted from the BIND 'rate-limit { responses-per-second N; ... }' block in named.conf.options (ISC RRL): true when a rate-limit block caps identical responses per client-prefix per second. False (no rate-limit block) leaves response volume unbounded, so the server is an unmitigated reflector for DNS amplification. An internet-facing server should have this configured.

minimal_responses_enabled.title: Minimal Responses Enabled
minimal_responses_enabled.description: Interpreted from BIND 'minimal-responses' in named.conf.options: true when minimal-responses yes; (or no-auth-recursive) trims unnecessary Additional/Authority records, shrinking response size and thus the amplification factor. False (minimal-responses no;) on a public server yields larger responses, increasing amplification gain when abused as a reflector. Secondary amplification-surface facet that compounds the absence of rate limiting.

zone_transfer_unrestricted.title: Zone Transfer Unrestricted
zone_transfer_unrestricted.description: Interpreted from the allow-transfer directive in named.conf.local / named.conf.options. True when zone transfers (AXFR/IXFR) are open to any client (allow-transfer { any; }) or the directive is absent on an authoritative zone, so anyone can pull the full zone and enumerate the internal namespace (hostnames, internal IPs). False (secure) when allow-transfer is { none; } or scoped to an explicit secondary-IP/key ACL. Interpreted boolean because the raw allow-transfer value is a composite address-match/key directive that cannot be safely substring-matched.

tsig_authenticated_transfers.title: TSIG-Authenticated Zone Transfers
tsig_authenticated_transfers.description: Interpreted: whether AXFR/IXFR zone transfers are authenticated with a TSIG HMAC shared secret (a key clause referenced from allow-transfer or the matching server stanza, e.g. allow-transfer { key transfer-key; }; with key "..." { algorithm hmac-sha256; secret ...; };). True (secure) when a TSIG key gates transfers; false when transfers are gated only by raw, spoofable source-IP ACLs or not authenticated at all — an attacker can impersonate a secondary's source IP to pull the zone. Interpreted boolean to avoid substring-matching the composite key/transfer directives.

transfers_gated_by_ip_only.title: Transfers Gated By IP Only
transfers_gated_by_ip_only.description: Interpreted: whether primary->secondary zone transfers are permitted solely on the basis of a raw source-IP address-match list (allow-transfer { <secondary-ip>; };) with no TSIG key requirement, so an attacker who can spoof a known secondary's source address can pull the zone. True when trust rests on IP alone; combined with tsig_authenticated_transfers=false this is the spoofable-trust exposure.

tsig_authenticated_notify.title: TSIG-Authenticated NOTIFY
tsig_authenticated_notify.description: Interpreted: whether NOTIFY/also-notify messaging between primary and secondaries is authenticated with a TSIG HMAC key (a key referenced from the server stanza covering the also-notify targets), so a spoofed NOTIFY cannot inject a forged zone-change/serial-bump signal. True when NOTIFY transactions carry TSIG; false when NOTIFY is gated only by source IP or unauthenticated.

dns_query_logging_enabled.title: DNS Query Logging Enabled
dns_query_logging_enabled.description: Whether the DNS server maintains a query audit trail (BIND 'querylog yes;' or a logging{} channel for the 'queries' category, per named.conf). Off by default for performance (~10x overhead). When false, high-entropy / high-volume subdomain lookups used for DNS tunneling and C2 leave no record and slip past egress filtering unobserved — the primary detection surface for exfiltration over DNS is gone.

access_audit_trail_enabled.title: Access Audit Trail Enabled
access_audit_trail_enabled.description: Shared workspace attestation: an audit trail of access/resolution events is captured for this component. When false there is no record from which DNS tunneling or exfiltration patterns could be reconstructed, so encoded-data lookups go undetected.

logs_stored_on_separate_system.title: Logs Stored On Separate System
logs_stored_on_separate_system.description: Shared workspace attestation: query/audit logs are shipped off-box to a separate system. The vector turns on logs being shipped off-box for anomaly analysis; when false, logs live only on the resolver (tamper-prone, not centrally analyzed) so high-volume/high-entropy DNS tunneling is never correlated and detected.

security_events_fully_logged.title: Security Events Fully Logged
security_events_fully_logged.description: Shared workspace attestation: security-relevant events are fully captured (not sampled/truncated). When false, the partial record leaves gaps an adversary can exfiltrate through, leaving DNS C2/tunneling activity unobserved.

rndc_bound_to_loopback_only.title: rndc Bound To Loopback Only
rndc_bound_to_loopback_only.description: Interpreted boolean: true only when the BIND controls{} block binds the rndc administrative channel to a loopback/trusted address (e.g. inet 127.0.0.1 allow { localhost; }). False when the control channel is bound to a non-loopback / routable address. A false value fires this exposure — an internet-reachable rndc channel permits remote nameserver takeover (reconfigure recursion, dump/flush cache, stop the service).

rndc_key_configured.title: rndc Key Configured
rndc_key_configured.description: Interpreted boolean: true only when the rndc control channel requires an HMAC shared-secret key — the controls{} inet stanza carries a keys{ "rndc-key"; } clause backed by a key { algorithm hmac-sha256; secret ...; } definition. False when no keys clause gates the channel (unauthenticated control). A false value fires this exposure — an unauthenticated rndc channel lets any client that can reach it issue administrative commands.

version_string_disclosed.title: Version String Disclosed
version_string_disclosed.description: Interpreted from the BIND 'version' directive in named.conf.options. True when no 'version none;' (or non-informative string) is set, so the version.bind CHAOS TXT query returns the precise named build (e.g. "9.18.x"), letting an attacker match the server against known CVEs. Secure when 'version none;'/'version "";' is present (dig @<server> version.bind CHAOS TXT +short returns empty/refused/generic).

listener_bound_to_any.title: Listener Bound To Any Interface
listener_bound_to_any.description: Interpreted from the BIND 'listen-on'/'listen-on-v6' directives in named.conf.options. True when named binds to all interfaces ('listen-on { any; }') on a server meant to be internal-only, widening the reachable attack surface beyond its intended networks. Secure when the listen-on list is an explicit interface set scoped to intended networks (e.g. listen-on { 127.0.0.1; 10.0.0.5; }).
